title: Elements of a study and sampling
statement: I can identify the basic elements of a statistical study and components of a good sample.
subskills: Identify the population, sample, experimental/observational units, parameter, and statistic. | Evaluate whether the sampling technique resulted in a representative sample and explain why random selection is important in sampling.

title: Classifying variables
statement: I can classify variables and relate them to potential statistical studies.
subskills: Classify variables as quantitative or categorical. | Determine potential explanatory variables that explain variability in a response variable.

title: Types of studies
statement: I can identify and evaluate different types of studies to determine the types of conclusions that can be made.
subskills: Distinguish the difference between observational studies and well-designed experiments. | Evaluate whether a cause-effect association can be made and explain why random assignment is important in the design of a study.

title: Categorical displays
statement: I can produce graphical displays and numerical summaries and interpret what graphs do and do not reveal for categorical data.
subskills: Produce graphical displays and numerical summaries for categorical variables. | Interpret what graphs (including bar charts and pie charts) reveal or identify aspects not revealed in a graph. | Analyze stacked bar charts, side-by-side pie charts and bar charts, and frequency and relative frequency tables.

title: Quantitative displays
statement: I can produce graphical displays and numerical summaries and interpret what graphs do and do not reveal for quantitative data.
subskills: Produce graphical displays and numerical summaries for quantitative data. | Interpret what graphs (including dot plots, histograms, and boxplots) reveal or identify aspects not revealed in a graph.

title: Center and variability
statement: I can use measures of central tendency and variability to summarize, describe, and compare distributions.
subskills: Calculate, interpret, and compare common measures of central tendency (mean, median, and mode). | Calculate, interpret, and compare common measures of variability (standard deviation, range, and IQR). | Describe the shape of a distribution, including unusual features and outliers, and interpret what this means in context.
art_of_stat_note: Summary statistics (mean, median, standard deviation, five-number summary, IQR)

title: Z-scores
statement: I can calculate z-scores and interpret them in various applications.
subskills: Calculate and interpret standardized z-scores as the number of standard deviations from the mean. | Use a z-score to determine if a value is unusual. | Use z-scores to compare values from different populations.

title: Basic probability
statement: I can calculate and interpret basic probabilities.
subskills: Calculate probabilities from a contingency table, including compound events (or/and) and conditional probabilities. | Use probability to determine if a random event is unusual.

title: Expected value
statement: I can calculate and interpret the expected value of a discrete probability distribution.
subskills: Set up a discrete probability distribution table to represent a scenario. | Calculate the expected value and standard deviation of a discrete probability distribution and interpret the results.

title: Binomial distribution
statement: I can identify and use the binomial distribution to calculate probabilities and use in applications.
subskills: Define a binomial random variable to represent an experiment or verify properties of a random variable is binomial. | Calculate probabilities and boundaries using the binomial distribution. | Calculate the mean and standard deviation to determine unusual events.

title: Normal distribution
statement: I can identify and use the normal distribution to calculate probabilities and use in applications.
subskills: Identify when a random variable can be modeled by the normal distribution. | Calculate probabilities and boundaries using the normal distribution.

title: Central Limit Theorem
statement: I can apply the Central Limit Theorem (CLT) to means and proportions.
subskills: Identify the mean and standard deviation of a sampling distribution of means and proportions, and evaluate whether the CLT applies. | Calculate probabilities for sampling distributions of means and proportions using the CLT.
art_of_stat_note: Not yet covered: sampling distributions and CLT probabilities. The Unit 2 FAQ has a navigation guide.

title: Confidence interval structure
statement: I can describe and apply the formulation of a confidence interval.
subskills: Calculate and explain the terms and symbols used to construct a confidence interval. | Interpret the margin of error as the amount of variability we expect to see in our estimate. | Determine the sample size needed to achieve a given margin of error.
art_of_stat_note: Confidence interval entries are listed under S14. Margin of error and sample size are not yet covered.

title: Confidence intervals for means and proportions
statement: I can calculate and interpret confidence interval estimates for means and proportions.
subskills: Write a research question about a parameter that can be estimated using a one-proportion z interval or a one-mean t interval. | Calculate the boundaries of a confidence interval. | Interpret the confidence interval estimates for means and proportions in context.

title: Choosing z or t tests
statement: I can apply one-sample z tests or t tests appropriately.
subskills: Explain when a z test or t test is appropriate. | Identify the proper test when presented with a scenario. | Write a research question with a claim that can be tested using a one-proportion z test or a one-mean t test.

title: Conducting one-sample tests
statement: I can conduct a one-sample test and interpret the conclusion.
subskills: Identify when a z test or t test is appropriate. | Set up and conduct a one-proportion z test and one-mean t test and write a valid conclusion in context. | Verify the statistical assumptions and conditions based on sound statistical practices, including sample size.
art_of_stat_note: One-proportion z-test. The one-mean t-test is not yet in the hub.

title: Type I and II errors
statement: I can evaluate possible errors due to sampling.
subskills: Describe a Type I and Type II error in context. | Evaluate potential consequences for a Type I and Type II error. | Describe how the level of significance and sample size can affect the probability of a Type I and Type II error, and the power of a test.

title: Informal inference
statement: I can draw conclusions from graphical and numerical summaries of a relationship between variables using informal inference.
subskills: Draw conclusions from graphical and numerical summaries of a relationship between variables using informal inference.

title: Choosing two-sample tests
statement: I can apply two-sample and paired tests in appropriate contexts.
subskills: Explain when each test is appropriate. | Identify the proper test when presented with a scenario. | Write a research question with a claim that can be tested using a two-proportion z test, two-mean t test, or paired t test.

title: Conducting two-sample tests
statement: I can set up, conduct, and interpret the final results of two-sample tests and matched pairs tests in appropriate contexts.
subskills: Set up and conduct a two-proportion z test, two-mean t test, and paired t test. | Verify the statistical assumptions and conditions based on sound statistical practices, including sample size.
art_of_stat_note: Independent two-sample t-test; Matched / paired t-test; Two-proportion z-interval; Two-proportion z-test

title: Choosing chi-square, ANOVA, regression
statement: I can apply chi-square tests, ANOVA, and linear regression in appropriate contexts.
subskills: Explain when each test is appropriate. | Identify the proper test when presented with a scenario. | Write a research question with a claim that can be tested using a chi-squared GOF, chi-square test for independence, ANOVA, or linear regression t test.

title: Conducting those tests
statement: I can set up, conduct, and interpret the final results of chi-square tests, ANOVA, and linear regression in appropriate contexts.
subskills: Set up and conduct a chi-squared GOF, chi-square test for independence, ANOVA, and linear regression t test. | Verify the statistical assumptions and conditions based on sound statistical practices, including sample size.
art_of_stat_note: Chi-square goodness-of-fit; Chi-square test of independence; One-way ANOVA

title: Scatterplots and regression
statement: I can interpret scatterplots and linear regression outputs, including correlation, coefficient of determination, and slope.
subskills: Evaluate the direction, form, and strength of a scatterplot visually and with numerical summaries. | Interpret the slope and y-intercept of a linear regression equation in context.
